text:
maya_g: Hey benefits team — quick question. I'm starting a fertility med (injectable Gonal-F + Lupron) next month. Plan is Redwood Gold PPO. Pharmacy told me it needs prior auth and ships from a specialty pharmacy that isn't in-network locally. Can benefits confirm coverage + whether Redwood will cover specialty pharmacy dispensing fees? Also worried about timing — meds must start day-of-cycle in 10 days. Thanks 🙏
benefits-bot: Reminder: For PHI, please DM or submit via benefits portal. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/prior-auth
alex_k: Hi @maya_g — can you DM me the member ID? I can pull plan details. Specialty meds often have a PA window (7–10 business days) but we can request expedited review for medical necessity.
maya_g: DMed you the last 4 + DOB. Also provider submitted a prior auth but pharmacy says paperwork incomplete (needs ICD and start date).
ben_r: I'll take this — pinged the carrier rep. Two quick notes: 1) Some carriers cover injectables under medical benefit (J-codes) instead of pharmacy — if provider bills via office, that avoids specialty pharmacy copays. 2) We'll request an expedited review citing 'time-sensitive infertility treatment'.
emily_p: FYI, here's the intake checklist I use: 
```
- Member ID + DOB
- Provider NPI
- Diagnosis code (e.g., N97.x)
- Proposed start date
- Medical justification letter (1–2 paragraphs)
```
I'll attach sample justification in the portal.
benefits-bot: Submitted expedited request to carrier #ACME1234 — estimated turnaround 48–72 hours. You should also get an email confirmation from carrier. If denied, we can file an internal appeal. Portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/appeals
maya_g: Thanks team! If carrier says 'not covered' my out-of-pocket for specialty pharmacy was quoted $950. If moved to medical claim/how does cost-sharing work? Also any paperwork to waive deductibles for fertility?
alex_k: Good q. If billed under medical benefit and your plan's medical deductible/coinsurance applies; sometimes fertility has separate limits — Redwood Gold has fertility rider that covers diagnostics and treatment with 20% coinsurance after deductible. We can escalate to plan admin to check if meds qualify under the rider. I'll confirm by EOD.
ben_r: Carrier replied — they requested the provider fill in 'treatment timeline' and confirm procedure code. I've DM'd the provider contact and attached a one-paragraph template for clinical justification. Maya, we put 'expedite' in notes. Will update thread when carrier confirms coverage type.
maya_g: :thumbsup: really appreciate it. If you need me to sign anything or call pharmacy, I'll do it. Also open to switching to medical billing if that lowers cost.
